standard.title: Create artworks reflecting personal expression
standard.description: select and manipulate visual conventions, visual arts processes and/or materials to create artworks that reflect personal expression, and represent and/or challenge, ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and create artworks with coordinated visual choices and can evaluate feedback in their practice. They make deliberate aesthetic decisions. They have not yet developed a sustained personal voice, self-initiated research process, or created artworks that deliberately challenge established perspectives.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select and manipulate visual conventions, processes and materials to create artworks that reflect personal expression and represent or challenge ideas, perspectives and meaning.

nodes.label: Researching and developing personal approaches
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can research approaches to their subject or concept and develop a direction that reflects a personal point of view — not just reproducing a known style.
nodes.minimum_width: Research at least two approaches to representing a subject or concept; identify one that resonates with a personal point of view and explain why.
nodes.typical_width: Research approaches to representing subjects and concepts from particular viewpoints; annotate research with own images and written evaluations; develop a personal direction distinct from direct imitation; document the development of personal expression.
wider: Investigate how artists across cultures represent similar themes from distinctly different viewpoints — analyse how personal, cultural and contextual factors shape the approach; develop a response that reflects your own position
Explore how visual arts can represent personal experiences — investigate how other artists have approached self-awareness, emotional awareness or wellbeing; develop your own approach
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who research only to imitate rather than to find a personal direction produce technically competent work without personal expression — the descriptor explicitly requires expression, and without self-directed research the work stays in exemplar convergence.

response_modes.reason: Developing a personal point of view from research requires explicit reasoning — 'Why does this approach resonate? What does it allow me to do that others don't?' Without this reasoning scaffold, students default to whichever approach looks most achievable.

success_criteria: Researches at least two approaches to representing a subject or concept
Identifies one that reflects a personal point of view and gives a specific reason

nodes.label: Creative problem-solving and resolution
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate and use creative problem-solving to resolve visual and conceptual challenges throughout the making process.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one creative challenge in a work in progress and document at least two possible solutions before choosing one.
nodes.typical_width: Use creative problem-solving throughout the making process; document challenges and multiple possible resolutions; make and justify choices; track how problems were resolved in final documentation.
wider: Create an artwork that represents a current global or local issue — research how other artists have addressed similar themes; develop a distinct visual argument; evaluate whether the work challenges or represents the issue
Create a site-specific 3D work — document how site conditions posed challenges and how you resolved them through sculptural techniques, space and form

response_modes.reason: Creative problem-solving is context-dependent — the problems differ across media, concepts and sites. Students who have only problem-solved in one context develop narrow strategies. A range of challenge types builds genuine creative resourcefulness.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Socially engaged (issue-based) and site-specific challenges each present types of creative problem unique to those contexts — students who engage with both develop substantially broader creative problem-solving capability.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one creative challenge in a work in progress
Documents at least two possible solutions before choosing one, with reasoning

nodes.label: Personal expression in completed artworks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create artworks in which personal expression is evident — using materials, techniques and conventions in intentional, interpretative and personal ways to represent or challenge ideas, perspectives and meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Create one artwork that reflects a personal position and uses at least two visual choices (convention, material, technique) in ways that are intentional and interpretative.
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks that realise planned intentions and communicate personal expression; use materials, techniques and conventions interpretatively; create works in response to specific subjects, themes or ideas; represent or challenge perspectives through visual means.
wider: Create artworks that deliberately challenge an established perspective or assumption — use research and documentation to show how the challenge is constructed visually
Apply painting techniques to create the illusion of texture and form in a landscape — document how technical decisions serve the expressive intent

response_modes.reason: Research, problem-solving and personal voice come together in the completed work. The integration is evidenced when the artwork reflects something distinctive — not a competent generic response but a personal interpretative position.

success_criteria: Creates an artwork that reflects a personal position or perspective
Uses at least two visual choices in ways that are interpretative — not merely technical — and can explain what personal meaning they carry
